Area.evidence_source: Most farmers reported protracted concerns about physical health before their death but continued to work. In addition to experiencing injury from farm-related incidents (ie, spinal injury and industrial auditory injury), they experienced gastroenterology disorders (eg, gastroesophageal reflux disease) and chronic pain (eg, osteoarthritis). Farmers were fearful of the future with regard to increasing health concerns and pharmacological treatment as health declined, inability to work, and experienced increasing pain, fatigue, and sleep difficulties; however, they were stoic in their resolve to continue farming.
